title: Panda's Parents' House
paragraphs: “Lhasa, I’d heard about you, but I’ve really met someone amazing.”
……From the way Panda speaks, it’s clear he’s connected to her. I’m a little curious about what kind of relationship they have.
“It’s work-related. I’ve been saying that all along, haven’t I? Dad.”
“Oh, right. My apologies. I just got so excited that you were back—it was my fault.”
“…Oh, come on. It’s fine, but I’d appreciate it if you didn’t get so worked up.”

He looks a little dejected… but this peacock Beastman has some incredibly flashy tail feathers. However, depending on his mood, his tail feathers keep opening and closing, standing up and lying down. Sakura-chan and Kou are watching those tail feathers with great curiosity.
“That’s sooo cool. His tail feathers flutter!”
“Flutter, flutter—”

Perhaps sensing their interest, the peacock beastman gives Sakura and Kou a gentle smile. Then, as if to entertain them, he spreads his tail feathers and raises and lowers both arms. It seems like a different kind of dance from the one Filolial-sama performs.
“Wow!”
“So fun!”
“Hehehe… Rasa, who are these kids?”
Hmm… It doesn’t seem like a bad peacock Beastman.
“They’re special monsters who live with the Shield Hero, and apparently, they used to be Filolials.”

With a “puff,” Sakura and Kou transform back into their Filolial-sama forms. The peacock beastman looks surprised at the sight, but immediately laughs back and pets Sakura-chan and the others. He seems like a nice person.
“Well, well—it seems there are still plenty of mysterious things in this world.”

Flapping its tail feathers open and closed to capture Sakura-chan and the others’ interest, the Peacock Beastman says this to Panda. To acknowledge it so immediately—it seems he has quite a flexible mindset. After all, there remains a world so deep it reaches the depths of Filolial-sama, Fitoria-tan… and even Filo-tan. The world is still brimming with mystery.
“That’s for sure.”
“I’m glad to see you’re not bored. Still, we—Lasa—are always rooting for your happiness. It might even be better than a job like being a mercenary.”
“I know that already!”

The panda replied with an expression that clearly said he found it a real hassle, and then… the entire settlement came together for a lively celebration. Amid the festive atmosphere of a banquet, the villagers—led by Father—performed one entertainment act after another to entertain us.

Father was chatting with an elderly panda—who seemed to be acting as the representative—while keeping an eye on the village children and others. As for me, I thoroughly enjoyed my time with Sakura-chan and the others, who were absolutely fascinated by the peacock Beastman. That peacock Beastman was actually quite a skilled dancer. It might even be worth using as a reference for her idol activities.

And now, she’s busy cooking up a storm in the temporary shelter—I guess she’s good at it. She seems quite skilled at decorative knife work. With hands like wings, she deftly holds the knife and slices the ingredients as if dancing in the air to arrange them beautifully. She’s also making a ramen-like dish using her secret soup. She’s really showing off her skills.
“Sometimes your movements remind me of Lars-chan’s in battle.”
“I’m aware I’m drawing inspiration from her style. Though mine’s just a hodgepodge of different fighting styles, really.”
“Also, you really give off a strong ‘master craftsman’ vibe.”
“Oh, my parents made a living doing that—traveling around and supporting me.”
“Traveling?”
“That’s right. I’m tired of hiding it, so I’ll tell you: my biological parents were caught up in the war and died. The guy cooking over there is the foster father who took me in and raised me.”
Panda said this with a completely unperturbed expression. She seems to have led quite a harrowing life.
“Huh? Then what about this village?”
“It’s just the hometown I finally managed to reach after all sorts of things happened.”
“Hmm… That war was tragic… Before we could join this settlement, the villages of our clan that we’d been in contact with got caught up in it… Everyone was scattered to the four winds.”
So replied the elderly panda—who appeared to be Panda’s grandfather—as he puffed on his tobacco pipe.

“As far as I’m concerned, those parents were my parents from the time I could remember. It’s thanks to them that I know the languages of so many different countries. I traveled all over looking for my hometown.”
“I see…”
“My parents were the kind who dabbled in all sorts of things, like business. I like to think I’ve developed a keen eye for things.”
“Whoa!”

The peacock beastman spreads his arms wide; he places a total of four bowls of what appears to be ramen on his hands and arms, and at the same moment, soup and noodles pour down from above, seemingly completing the dish. What a deft feat.

It reminds me of the scene with Father from my first world, who—while complaining that cooking was a hassle—would flick ingredients lightly before slicing them into multiple layers with a knife before they even hit the pot. He did it with such nonchalance, but perhaps that’s a skill only a chef without equal could pull off.
Hmm, could it be that this peacock Beastman is such a skilled cook that even Father would want to hire him?
“Father, isn’t the panda parent’s cooking just as good as yours?”
“I don’t think you should overestimate me, but he certainly puts on a show in the kitchen.”
“Thank you.”
The panda’s parent arranges the dishes in front of Father and the others and expresses their gratitude.
“Can you do all sorts of other things, too?”
“Compared to you heroes, it’s nothing special…”
“Don’t lie. You still have connections all over the place, don’t you?”
“Lasa… People support one another. And it’s precisely because we’ve built such good relationships that I was able to come to your hometown. I have to thank everyone.”
“Yeah, yeah.”
“Hmm… It might be fun to recruit you for the castle…”
“Please spare me. If that happens, I’m quitting this job and going back to being a freelance mercenary.”
“Lasa.”
The peacock beastman chimes in.
“I understand how embarrassed you are and why you don’t want to do this. So don’t worry—if you don’t want to go, I won’t make you.”
“Ugh, man, this guy is such a pain to deal with…”
As if he couldn’t stand it anymore, the panda is scratching his head vigorously. You’re going to go bald!

This is just like that, isn’t it? It’s probably the same feeling as when your parents come to parent-teacher day and everyone’s staring at you. You don’t like it, do you? I totally get it. I vaguely remember a rare occasion in elementary school when my parents actually came to school, too.

“I’m very pleased with the warm welcome I’ve received as the Shield Hero. So, as a token of my gratitude to Larsazusa, who’s always been there to help me, I’d like to do whatever I can to show my appreciation. I look forward to your continued support.”
The villagers are all looking at each other, unsure of how to respond. Soon, Father borrows the kitchen that the panda parents used and starts cooking.
“Father! You’re going to have a cooking showdown with the panda parents, aren’t you! You’re showing off your skills just to criticize them!”
“W-well, that’s…”
“Naofumi’s cooking is delicious, isn’t it?”
“Yeah. Iwatani’s cooking is delicious.”
Sakura-chan and the others chime in to the Peacock Beastman. There’s no doubt about it!
“That’s not it! Motoyasu-kun, don’t say things that might cause a misunderstanding!”
Father cautioned him, looking flustered. Was that a misunderstanding? So, Father… made fried rice and steamed buns to go with the ramen and served them up.
“Yay!”
“Iwatani’s cooking—we only get to eat it once in a while, so this is a real treat!”
“It’s definitely been a while.”

Sakura-chan and Éclair, who was traveling with us, agreed. Due to the domestic situation and other factors, Father rarely gets to cook. However, whenever he’s been feeling stressed, Father has occasionally been spotted in the kitchen. Only a select few—like me, Filolial-sama, Éclair, and Panda—get to eat those meals. I suppose he’s serving them up so publicly under the pretext that Panda’s been working hard.
“T-the dish made by the Shield Hero…”
The pandas in the settlement are gulping their saliva and staring at the food that’s been served.
“Please help yourselves before it gets cold.”
“Y-yes!”
“T-this has a different texture and flavor than what we usually eat!”
“What is this!?”
“What’s going on!?”
“It’s so easy to eat…!?”
The pandas were truly astonished.

I was watching from behind a corner—seeing Father casually mix ingredients like bamboo shoots into the dish and experiment with seasonings. Weapons skills aren’t everything. Father is constantly coming up with countless ingenious ideas in all sorts of places, often without even realizing it himself.

After that, perhaps because their tension had eased, the residents of the panda settlement seemed to fully enjoy the welcome feast in their own ways. As the sun set and everyone had fallen asleep, we ended up resting at Father’s family home—a large house even by the settlement’s standards. Oh, and since elephants aren’t allowed inside, I’m resting out by the barn with Kou. They say it’s deep in the mountains, but it’s not that cold, so we’ll be fine.
“Lars-chan”
“What is it?”
“Do you actually have a room of your own, Lars-chan?”
“I do, but you absolutely can’t go in there.”
“Okay. There are things I don’t want anyone to see, right? I’ve been there myself, so I get it.”

I get it, too. It’s only natural for a healthy young man to have a hentai magazine or two. By the way, I used to have a photo book of a pig I’d become friends with. Looking back now, it was total trash. Also, in the first world, my room was full of Filo-chan merchandise. I wouldn’t feel the least bit embarrassed if anyone else saw those, though.
Speaking of my room, I seem to recall Father from the first world saying something like, “It wasn’t good that Raphtalia saw my eroge…” Hmm, when was that again? My memory’s a bit fuzzy.
“You… I’m definitely going to make you cry someday, so you better be prepared.”
Panda seems to be directing some serious killing intent toward Father.
“I’m heading to my room for a bit, so don’t you dare come in.”
Panda went back to what appeared to be his own room, glancing back repeatedly as he went. I’m sure he’s hoarding all sorts of merchandise in there.
“That was a very meaningful time. It really made me realize how tense I’ve been lately with everything so tense and stressful.”
Éclair says as she sits down in front of the hearth.
“That’s true. All things considered, a lot has happened lately, hasn’t it?”
Father replies with a nostalgic air.
“I’ve always wanted to see the world, so I’m glad I got to come to Lars-chan’s hometown.”
Father was stroking Sakura-chan, who was snoring contentedly after a hearty meal. It was a picture-perfect scene. I absolutely can’t let Rival get the better of me here!
“To the Shield Hero and his party, thank you so much for bringing Larsazusa to our village today.”
The peacock beastman and the elderly panda bring tea and sit down by the hearth.
“No, no—we’re the ones who are grateful that you accommodated our sudden visit. How should I put it… Given who Lars-chan is, does it seem like he doesn’t come back here very often?”
“Yes… He keeps in touch regularly, but he rarely comes by. Especially in the last few years…”
“Just when we thought we’d finally found a place to settle down, he bolted out of here…”
The old panda looks a bit troubled, too.
“I see… It seems Lars-chan has been saving money. Could it be that she’s doing this so the people here can live comfortably?”
Oh? Father is asking the question straight out here. It’s a topic everyone’s been curious about, and I can sort of guess why.
“Lars-chan has helped us out in many ways, and since he fought bravely against the Shieldfreeden, I’ve heard that if there’s a valid reason, Siltvelt won’t hesitate to provide assistance.”
It sounded like Siltvelt was providing that kind of support.
“It’s true that money and supplies are sent to us from time to time. Lately, with government aid on top of that, life in this village has become easier than it used to be.”
“So that’s how it is, then…”
“However… since this isn’t an area plagued by extreme poverty, I think most of Lasa’s funds are being allocated elsewhere—thanks to my savings, connections, and my work as a traveling merchant.”
Father looked somewhat surprised. It seems the Peacock Beastman knows exactly how the money is being spent.

“That child is good at looking after others, but she’s not exactly straightforward. It’s only natural that someone like her would stick her nose into strange matters and wonder what the Shield Hero is using his stipend for.”
“No… I just assumed he was simply sending money back to his parents…”
“She’s been through a lot, you see. Ah… Come to think of it, everything that’s happened since I met her feels like it’s gone by so quickly…”

The peacock beastman says this with a look of nostalgia on his face. Given everything that’s happened, I’ve been trying not to dwell on it myself, but aren’t you thinking about your daughter a little too much? You’re incredibly overprotective. It practically looks like she ran away from home.

Judging by what you’ve said, this peacock Beastman must be a retired master chef and traveling merchant. I also suspect he’s quite knowledgeable about alchemy as well. Inside Panda’s parents’ house, there were all sorts of equipment and what looked like merchandise. There were even lights resembling aquariums containing faintly glowing jellyfish—the interior design is anything but boring.
Even though it’s deep in the mountains, isn’t this a pretty modern house? In a different sense, it might come in handy if we were to recruit him.
